answers: For Zion and Jerusalem
For the kings of the nations
For Jerusalem's enemies
easy.explanation: The prophet says, "For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest."
easy.q: For whose sake will the prophet not hold his peace?

answers: Jerusalem's walls
Zion's righteousness and glory
The watchmen on the walls
easy.explanation: The verse says, "The Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory."
easy.q: What will the Gentiles and kings see?

answers: A king rejoicing over victory
A watchman rejoicing over a city
A bridegroom rejoicing over a bride
easy.explanation: God's joy is compared to "the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride."
easy.q: What image describes God's joy over Jerusalem?

answers: They will shine openly and be visible to all
They will hide Jerusalem from the nations
They will come only after the city is destroyed
medium.explanation: Righteousness will go forth as brightness, and salvation as a burning lamp.
medium.q: How are Zion's righteousness and salvation described?

answers: Because the watchmen will rename it
Because the mouth of the Lord will name it
Because the kings of the nations will choose its name
medium.explanation: The verse says the new name will be one "which the mouth of the Lord shall name."
medium.q: Why will Jerusalem receive a new name?

answers: Forsaken and empty
Rich and fruitful
Surrounded by walls
medium.explanation: Desolate means abandoned or empty; Jerusalem's land will no longer be called that.
medium.q: What does the word "Desolate" mean in this passage?

answers: A change from honor to abandonment
A change from forsakenness to love, honor, and renewal
A change from holiness to enemy rule
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from names such as Forsaken and Desolate to names expressing delight, marriage, and restoration.
challenge.q: What change is described throughout these verses?

answers: God's relationship with Jerusalem is described with love and joy
Jerusalem will leave her land
The city will be rebuilt only for war
challenge.explanation: The bridegroom and bride image emphasizes affection, covenant relationship, and rejoicing.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the comparison of Jerusalem to a bride?

answers: The land will remain desolate and therefore receive honor
The land will be inhabited and fruitful, so it will no longer be called forsaken
The fruitfulness will cause the nations to destroy the land
challenge.explanation: The land is called Beulah, and its sons will marry it, contrasting with the former description of desolation.
challenge.q: How are the honor of Jerusalem and the fruitfulness of her land connected?

short_answers.question: What two names will Jerusalem no longer be called?
short_answers.explanation: Isaiah 62:4 says, "Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate."

paragraphs.title: The Watchmen and Prayer Until Redemption

answers: Upon Jerusalem's walls
At the gates of a distant land
In the courts of foreign kings
easy.explanation: The Lord says, "I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem."

answers: Only during the day
Only during the night
Day and night
easy.explanation: They "shall never hold their peace day nor night."
easy.q: When do the watchmen continue without ceasing?

answers: Her enemies will eat and drink them
Those who gathered them will eat and drink them
They will remain unused
easy.explanation: The Lord promises that the gatherers will eat the corn and drink the wine.
easy.q: What will happen to Jerusalem's corn and wine?

answers: To fight every enemy
To make mention of the Lord and pray until redemption
To gather the harvest from the fields
medium.explanation: The watchmen are told to make mention of the Lord and give Him no rest until Jerusalem is established.
medium.q: What is the main role of the watchmen in this passage?

answers: So Jerusalem will become a praise in the earth
So the enemies will be warned of war
So everyone will know that the harvest is lost
medium.explanation: They must continue until the Lord makes Jerusalem "a praise in the earth."
medium.q: Why are the watchmen told not to be silent?

answers: Remain silent
Celebrate loudly
Guard the gates
medium.explanation: To hold one's peace means to remain silent; the watchmen are told not to stop speaking or praying.
medium.q: What does the phrase "hold their peace" mean in this passage?

answers: Formerly enemies consumed the harvest, but afterward the gatherers will enjoy it
Formerly Jerusalem was full, but afterward it will be desolate
Formerly there was no harvest, and afterward there will still be none
challenge.explanation: The Lord swears that the corn and wine will no longer be given to enemies but will be enjoyed by those who gathered them.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in verses 8–9?

answers: They ensure that the enemies receive the harvest
Their prayer continues until God's promise of security and blessing is fulfilled
They replace the workers who gather the harvest
challenge.explanation: The watchmen give the Lord no rest until Jerusalem is established and blessed.
challenge.q: How are the watchmen connected with the promise concerning the harvest?

answers: It places the celebration in a holy and joyful setting
It says the meal takes place secretly outside Jerusalem
It shows that only foreign kings may enjoy the harvest
challenge.explanation: The gathered produce is enjoyed in the courts associated with God's holiness.
challenge.q: What does the phrase "in the courts of my holiness" add to the description of eating and drinking?

short_answers.question: What must the watchmen give the Lord until Jerusalem is established?
short_answers.explanation: They are told to "give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth."

paragraphs.title: Preparing the Way and Israel's Return to Zion

answers: Prepare it, build up the highway, and remove the stones
Hide it from the nations
Leave it blocked
easy.explanation: They are told to prepare the way, cast up the highway, and gather out the stones.
easy.q: What are the people commanded to do to the way?

answers: That salvation is coming
That war is beginning
That Jerusalem has been abandoned
easy.explanation: The proclamation says, "Behold, thy salvation cometh."
easy.q: What does the Lord proclaim to the end of the world?

answers: The people of war
The holy people
The people of desolation
easy.explanation: They will be called "The holy people, The redeemed of the Lord."
easy.q: By what name will Israel be called?

answers: To make possible the people's return to Zion
To keep Jerusalem away from the nations
To hide the message of redemption
medium.explanation: Preparing the way is connected with the public announcement of the people's return and salvation.
medium.q: Why must the way be prepared and obstacles removed?

answers: To mark the place of a battle
To draw attention to the announcement of return and redemption
To announce that there is no way to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The standard is raised as part of the public preparation and proclamation to the nations.
medium.q: What is the purpose of lifting up a standard for the people?

answers: That the city has been abandoned
That the city is sought and valued again
That no one may enter the city
medium.explanation: Sought out shows that Jerusalem is no longer forsaken but is sought after and restored.
medium.q: What does the name "Sought out" communicate about Jerusalem?

answers: Preparing the way, announcing salvation, and receiving names of holiness and redemption
Destroying the city, scattering the people, and hiding the message
Gathering the harvest, building the walls, and changing the kings' names
challenge.explanation: The passage first prepares the road, then announces salvation, and finally describes the restored names of the people and city.
challenge.q: What order of ideas appears in verses 10–12?

answers: Both express the end of abandonment and the beginning of redemption
Both describe victory by Jerusalem's enemies
Both indicate that the road has been blocked
challenge.explanation: The redeemed people and the city not forsaken both signify restoration and deliverance.
challenge.q: How are "The redeemed of the Lord" and "A city not forsaken" related?

answers: The redemption is presented as a broad and public announcement
The salvation is intended only for the watchmen
The way to Jerusalem will remain closed to everyone
challenge.explanation: The proclamation reaches the ends of the earth, showing that the message is public and far-reaching.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the message being proclaimed "unto the end of the world"?

short_answers.question: What two names are given to the restored city?
short_answers.answer: Sought out and A city not forsaken.
short_answers.explanation: The final verse says, "thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken."
